origin.description: Create a style function from a builtin name, an R color name, a #rrggbb string, or RGB channels.
origin.usage: make_style(..., bg = FALSE, grey = FALSE, colors = num_colors())

arguments.text: One style. A name creates an entry in styles() as well as the function.

arguments.name: bg
arguments.text: Apply the color to the background.

arguments.name: grey
arguments.text: Use the 24-step ANSI grey ramp. Ignored when fewer than 256 colors are requested.

arguments.name: colors
arguments.text: How many colors to bake. Below 256, the nearest of the eight ANSI colors is used.

origin.details: The open and close codes are chosen when make_style runs. Calling the function later only wraps text, and it wraps only when num_ansi_colors() is greater than 1. An 8-digit hex color is accepted and its alpha byte is ignored. A builtin name such as red stays that builtin; with bg TRUE, red becomes bgRed.
origin.example:
pink <- make_style("pink", colors = 256)
cat(pink("pink"), "\n", sep="")
cat(make_style("yellow3", colors = 8)("eight"), "\n", sep="")

translation.description: Create a style function from a builtin name, an R color name, a #rrggbb string, or RGB channels.

arguments.name: spec
arguments.text: A builtin name, an R color name, #rrggbb, or three or four channel numbers.

arguments.name: bg
arguments.text: Apply the color to the background.

arguments.name: grey
arguments.text: Use the ANSI grey ramp when at least 256 colors are requested.

arguments.name: colors
arguments.text: Color count baked into the style. None uses num_colors().

arguments.name: named
arguments.text: One named argument also stores the style under that name.

translation.details: A sequence of three or four numbers stands in for the one-column RGB matrix. The baked codes do not change if num_colors() changes later. cli.palette remaps a builtin color at call time when at least 256 colors are enabled.
translation.example:
pink = make_style("pink", colors=256)
print(pink("pink"))
print(make_style("yellow3", colors=8)("eight"))
